boundary: Pass 5936 is a THEOREM about why the other lane's bridge is characteristic-2 only, proved by a one-line identity and confirmed by counts. Pass 5937 characterises the triple split on a 200/200 sample of each class, not exhaustively. Neither result claims novelty against the literature -- the char-2 symmetric/alternating coincidence is textbook

pass_5936_the_bridge_is_char_2_only.consequence: the polarization is SYMMETRIC at every q but ALTERNATING only in characteristic 2, where symmetric and alternating coincide. At odd q it defines a QUADRIC, not a symplectic space
pass_5936_the_bridge_is_char_2_only.identity: pol(M,M) = det(2M) - 2det(M) = 4det(M) - 2det(M) = 2det(M), which is nonzero exactly when det(M) is nonzero

q3_counts.check: the 16 singular classes are exactly Q+(3,3), which has (3+1)^2 = 16 points -- so the odd-q construction lands on the hyperbolic quadric, and their 9+6 becomes 16+24

pass_5936_the_bridge_is_char_2_only.significance: this turns their firewall from a caution into a theorem: the two-qubit doily picture is intrinsically characteristic 2 and there is no q=3 analogue to look for
pass_5936_the_bridge_is_char_2_only.the_question: does it lift to odd q?
pass_5936_the_bridge_is_char_2_only.their_result: det polarization on M_2(F_2) IS the two-qubit symplectic form, giving W(3,2)

pass_5937_the_triple_split.answer: the size of the common perp
pass_5937_the_triple_split.question: what separates the 360 triples from the 2880 in the q=3 heptad design?
pass_5937_the_triple_split.reading: a clean geometric invariant: three pairwise non-collinear points with FOUR common neighbours lie in 16 heptads; with ONE common neighbour, 33. The 2-design regularity fails at the triple level exactly along this perp-size dichotomy

pass_5938_joint_picture.q2: 3-design, lambda_3 = 1, six ovoids -- their doily census
pass_5938_joint_picture.q3: 2-design only, lambda_2 = 112, triples split 360/2880 by common-perp size 4 vs 1
pass_5938_joint_picture.so: the two-qubit picture and the heptad picture are not two views of one structure that survives all q -- they are the even and odd branches of the same computation, and the even branch has extra rigidity the odd branch lacks
pass_5938_joint_picture.why_q2_is_special: at q=2 W(3,q) HAS ovoids and the det polarization is symplectic; both facts are characteristic-2 accidents, and both fail at q=3
